# Independent audit: quantitative face exhaustion and linear buffer gap

Audited source:
`candidate 5dc06bb8226350eb`,
Sections 1--8. Result: **PASS**, with no repair identified.
The supplied exact checker was independently rerun and passes 1,316
calibration checks. The general geometric and variational implications
were checked separately from those finite examples.

## Actual input motion and near-face exhaustion

Replacing only input K_u by K_u+tB and taking the canonical hull is a
genuine compatible motion. Every anchored combination acquires a ball
displacement of radius at most t, proving both inclusions in (3), with
equality at the input base u. The printed inball and outer-radius
homotheties give the upper and lower mixed-volume constants (4)--(5).
Comparing first the measures and then the old-body threshold establishes
the uniform depth bound (6), including unbounded tilts and supporting
statuses. Pure-base caps need only the added-mass term.

If u lies outside a base face, no anchored representation of a point of
that face uses u. Its fibers stay fixed. A finite exposing base tilt
extends every face-restricted cap while excluding all other sampled
fibers, so ordinary depths on the face stay fixed as well. Thus a missed
input in Section 3 really keeps the old raw maximum Q unchanged. The
comparison is with the unrestricted ordinary infimum; it does not
incorrectly require the enlarged body to stay in one normalized compact
representative set. Constants and the strict contradiction g>=2g check.

## Uniform source and parameter bounds

The source inball lower bound gives Q>=q_*. Boundary depth is zero using
an actual finite sampled supporting roof; the ordinary continuous-mark
Lipschitz bound therefore places near-deepest marks in uniform own
inballs. For any u in the minimal face of p, an anchored representation
of p with a strictly positive coefficient at u exists. There are only
finitely many needed pairs. Concavity, nonnegativity, and one further
within-fiber inball interpolation prove (11)--(13) with the stated
constant. Log normalization then forces one chosen mark's parameter
value to be bounded below.

The source-ball lower bound for projective energy is valid: every
denominator admissible on the fiber is admissible on the contained ball,
whose energy at its center is exactly its volume. Every nonvertical cap
gets the stated own-ball strip increase. For completeness, the pure-base
margin used in Section 5 follows by perturbing a pure-base cap with
opposite continuous normals: their strict-base contributions agree,
while the two boundary-base contributions sum to the full boundary
mass. At least one has at most half that boundary mass. Consequently
the original pure-base mass exceeds ordinary depth by at least V_p/2.
This handles atomic caps without any regularity assumption.

## Joint value and row comparison

Combining the near-deepest error 2g/c_F with the positive strip gain and
the independent lower bound beta_epsilon>=beta_*+g gives exactly the two
envelopes in (17). Their minimum is c_B epsilon/H. This controls unknown
g/epsilon and is not a false transfer of a fixed-body estimate to moving
bodies. The global claim (18) correctly states its compact-positive
sublevel hypothesis and compares against all positive compatible bodies.
No derivative of an optimizing value is asserted.

In Section 8, a nonnegative affine contact majorant on sampled fibers is
also nonnegative on their canonical hull. The source barycenter confines
its row to the source's minimal base face. Applying the same interpolation
bound to that affine majorant yields L/L_i<=C_0 on the actual row.
Because the original-volume row has mass one, its relative entropy lies
between zero and log C_0. This is one-sided domination only, with no
asserted equality of the two row barycenters and no Gamma payment.
